subject: Michal Šimečka (Progressive Slovakia) and journalist Monika Tódová, apparently discussing rigging the election
called_fake_by: Michal Šimečka and the newspaper Denník N
claim: Two days before the national election, audio spread online in which Šimečka and a well-known journalist seemed to discuss buying votes. Both immediately said it was fake.
finding: AFP fact-checkers consulted experts who concluded the audio was AI-synthesized from real samples of their voices. The conversation never happened.
outcome: Šimečka's party lost to Robert Fico's. Some called it the first election swung by a deepfake. Researchers writing in the Harvard Misinformation Review argue that overstates it and point to deeper causes.

sources.title: Beyond the deepfake hype: AI, democracy, and "the Slovak case"
